seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 229 HTS Chapter 63 lines — blankets, bed sheets, pillowcases, towels, curtains, sacks, tarpaulins, tents, face masks and worn clothing — with General, FTA and Column 2 rates and the 2026 extra duty for China, India, Pakistan, Vietnam and others.

overview.intro:
Chapter 63 covers textile goods that are **made up** — cut, sewn or finished ready for use: **blankets** (6301), **bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen** such as sheets, pillowcases and towels (6302), **curtains** (6303), bedspreads and other furnishings (6304), **sacks and bags for packing goods** (6305), **tarpaulins, tents and sails** (6306), other made-up articles from cleaning cloths to face masks and flags (6307), needlecraft sets (6308), **worn clothing** (6309) and rags (6310). Its **229 lines** carry base rates from Free to **20.9%** (embroidered cotton bed linen); cotton towels are 9.1%–9.2% and most sheets 6.7%–11.4%.

On top of the base rate, since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Cambodia 10%, Vietnam and Türkiye 12.5%. **China pays 12.5% plus 7.5%** under List 4A on most lines, and **62.5%** on textile face masks and respirators. Worn clothing (6309) is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty for every country. Canada pays **50%** under Section 338 on synthetic curtains, plastic-strip sacks, tarpaulins and 6307.90.98 even with USMCA. The U.S. imported **$16.18B** of Chapter 63 goods in 2025: China $7.05B (44%), India $3.06B (19%), Pakistan $1.62B (10%) and Mexico $1.26B.

productGroups.label: Blankets and traveling rugs (incl. electric blankets)
productGroups.blurb: Blankets and traveling rugs by fibre: electric blankets 11.4%, cotton 8.4%, synthetic 8.5%, other 7.2%, wool Free. Quilts and comforters that are stuffed are not here — they are bedding of heading 9404.

productGroups.label: Bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen (sheets, pillowcases, towels)
productGroups.blurb: The largest heading: sheets, pillowcases and duvet covers, tablecloths and napkins, bath, beach and kitchen towels. Rates turn on fibre, print, nap and trim — from 2.5% (napped printed cotton) to 20.9% (embroidered or trimmed cotton, not napped); cotton terry towels are 9.1%.

productGroups.label: Curtains, drapes and interior blinds
productGroups.blurb: Curtains, drapes, valances and interior blinds of textiles, knitted or woven: 6.4% to 11.3%. Shower curtains of plastic sheeting are not here (chapter 39); textile shower curtains are.

productGroups.label: Bedspreads and other furnishing articles (not stuffed)
productGroups.blurb: Bedspreads, cushion covers, wall hangings, mattress covers and other furnishings that are not stuffed (stuffed cushions and pillows go to 9404); 3.2% to 14.9%, with hand-loomed and folklore items at 3.8%.

productGroups.label: Sacks and bags for packing goods (incl. FIBCs, woven PP sacks)
productGroups.blurb: Sacks and bags used to pack and ship goods: jute sacks Free, cotton 6.2%, flexible intermediate bulk containers (FIBCs) and woven polypropylene or polyethylene sacks 8.4%. Laminated woven sacks from China and Vietnam are under antidumping and countervailing duty orders. Shopping and tote bags are heading 4202.

productGroups.label: Tarpaulins, awnings, tents, sails, camping goods
productGroups.blurb: Tarpaulins, awnings and sunblinds, tents and canopies, sails, air mattresses and other camping goods. Backpacking tents and sails are Free; synthetic tarps and other synthetic tents 8.8%. Plastic-film tarps are chapter 39.

productGroups.label: Other made-up articles (cleaning cloths, masks, flags, pet toys)
productGroups.blurb: Everything made up and not named elsewhere: floor and dish cloths, lifejackets, labels, surgical drapes, pet toys, flags, textile face masks and respirators, and the catch-all 6307.90.98 (7%). Chinese masks and respirators pay a 50% Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Needlecraft sets (fabric and yarn for rugs, tapestries)
productGroups.blurb: Needlecraft sets of woven fabric and yarn for making rugs, tapestries, embroidered tablecloths or similar, put up for retail sale: 11.4%.

productGroups.label: Worn clothing and other worn textile articles
productGroups.blurb: Worn clothing, blankets, linen, furnishings, footwear and headgear showing appreciable wear and entered in bulk, bales or sacks (chapter note 3). Free, and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty for every country (note 52(b)).

productGroups.label: Rags, scrap twine, cordage and rope
productGroups.blurb: Used or new rags and scrap twine, cordage and rope, sorted or not. Free, except unsorted rags of wool (5.5¢/kg).

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.body: Printed cotton bed linen without trim, not napped, is 6.7%. China adds 7.5% under List 4A (9903.88.15) and 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31): 26.7% in all, **$2,670** on a $10,000 shipment. The same sheets from India pay 16.7% ($1,670).

workedExamples.title: Disposable textile face masks from China
workedExamples.body: 6307.90.98 is 7%. Since January 1, 2026 Chinese textile face masks and respirators pay 50% under the 2024 four-year review (9903.91.07) — in place of List 4A — plus 12.5% (9903.05.31): 69.5% in all, **$6,950** on $10,000.

workedExamples.title: Polypropylene tarpaulin from Canada, with a USMCA claim

workedExamples.title: Bales of used clothing from Canada

A $10,000 shipment from any country but China pays **$0**; China's List 4A adds 7.5% ($750).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Subchapter I (headings 6301–6307) applies only to made-up articles, of any textile fabric.

**Note 2.** Subchapter I does not cover goods of chapters 56 to 62, or worn clothing and other worn articles of heading 6309.

**Note 3.** Heading 6309 covers only: (a) articles of textile materials — clothing and clothing accessories and parts; blankets and traveling rugs; bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen; furnishings other than carpets of 5701–5705 and tapestries of 5805 — and (b) footwear and headgear of any material other than asbestos. They must both **show signs of appreciable wear** and be **entered in bulk or in bales, sacks or similar packings**.

**Subheading note 1.** Subheading 6304.20 covers articles of warp-knit fabric impregnated or coated with alpha-cypermethrin, chlorfenapyr, deltamethrin, lambda-cyhalothrin, permethrin or pirimiphos-methyl (insecticide bed nets).

**Section XI notes that decide Chapter 63.** Note 7: "made up" means, among others, cut other than into squares or rectangles, finished ready for use without sewing (dusters, towels, tablecloths, blankets), hemmed or with a knotted fringe, or assembled by sewing. Note 1 sends textile articles of heading 4202 (shopping bags, travel bags), chapter 94 (stuffed bedding: quilts, pillows, cushions) and chapter 95 (toys) out of Section XI.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
Chapter 63 has no additional U.S. notes of its own; the Section XI notes apply.

**Section XI additional U.S. note 2.** "Certified hand-loomed and folklore" products (6304.99.10, 6304.99.40) are those certified by an official of the producing country's government under procedures established by USTR.

**Footnote 1/.** Lines marked 1/ (for example 6301.30, 6302.10, 6302.21) point to heading 9903.90.08: products of Russia pay 35% in place of the column 2 rate on them.

**Statistical notes.** The three-digit numbers in brackets (for example 363 cotton terry towels, 666 man-made-fibre furnishings) are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 63 imports since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, China List 4A and the 50% on masks, Canada's Section 338 duty and the laminated woven sack orders.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 229 Chapter 63 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties — up to 50% on Indian sheets and towels — **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**; only Jordan's exception list and CAFTA-DR claims (notes 52(i)–(j)) cover Chapter 63, and worn clothing is exempt everywhere. China keeps List 4A (7.5%) and, since January 1, 2026, pays **50%** on textile face masks and respirators. Since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on five subheadings, USMCA or not.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 63 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 4A, its product exclusions and the 2024 four-year-review rate on masks, the Canada Section 338 duty, Russia's rates in place of column 2, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on laminated woven sacks (China, Vietnam) and narrow woven ribbons (China, Taiwan) are explained below; no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 63 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 301 (China, 2018-2019 lists) + Section 301 (China, 2024 four-year review)
inEffect.exemption: List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15, since February 14, 2020) covers 75 of the chapter's 99 eight-digit subheadings; the rest — electric and synthetic blankets (6301.10, 6301.40, 6301.90), man-made-fibre bed linen (6302.22, 6302.32), cotton damask table linen (6302.51.10), man-made-fibre towels (6302.93), some curtains and bedspreads (6303.92.10, 6304.11.20–.30, 6304.19.15–.20, 6304.93), synthetic tarpaulins and other tents (6306.12, 6306.29), 6306.90, lifejackets (6307.20), pet toys (6307.90.75) and surgical and cotton pile towels (6307.90.89) — were on List 4B, which never took effect. The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) on every line but worn clothing (note 52(b)). N95 and other textile respirators and face masks (6307.90.98.42/.44/.50/.70/.75) pay 50% under the 2024 four-year review (9903.91.07) instead of List 4A. Four List 4A exclusions (9903.88.69, note 20(vvv)(iv)) run through November 9, 2026: knitted polyester dust covers for mattresses and pillows (6302.10.00.20), zippered cotton pillow protectors (6302.31.90.40), and instant cold packs and cotton laparotomy sponges (6307.90.98.91). The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most Chinese cotton sheets, towels, blankets and tarps pay 20% on top of the base rate; synthetic blankets, polyester sheets and synthetic tarps pay 12.5%; masks and respirators 62.5%; worn clothing 7.5%.

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list; only worn clothing (6309) is exempt (note 52(b)). GSP (SPI A, A*), still printed on a few lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian sheets, towels and furnishings pay the base rate plus 10%: 16.7% on printed cotton sheets, 19.1% on cotton terry towels.

inEffect.exemption: Pakistan has no exception list; only worn clothing is exempt (note 52(b)). GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Pakistani towels and bed linen pay the base rate plus 10%: 19.1% on cotton terry towels.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94). Under USMCA (General Note 11) a Chapter 63 good qualifies only if its fabric is from the region and it is cut and sewn there. The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican made-ups pay nothing extra with a valid USMCA claim; without one, the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Vietnam has no exception list for Chapter 63. Laminated woven sacks from Vietnam (6305.33.00.40/.80) also pay antidumping and countervailing duties, continued in November 2024. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese bedding, curtains and tents pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Türkiye has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Turkish towels and bedding pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Cambodia's exception list (note 52(j)(5), 9903.06.02) names no Chapter 63 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Cambodian made-ups pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Bangladesh's exception list (note 52(j)) names no Chapter 63 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Bangladeshi towels, bed linen and bags pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of the base rate (note 52(k)), so lines with a base rate of 10% or more (for example 11.3% curtains, 20.9% embroidered cotton sheets) pay only the base rate. The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2)) names no Chapter 63 subheading; worn clothing is exempt. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Portuguese and other EU sheets and towels pay 10% in total, or the base rate where it is higher.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on 6303.92.20 (synthetic curtains), 6305.33.00 (polyethylene/polypropylene sacks), 6306.12.00 (synthetic tarpaulins), 6306.19.21 (tarpaulins of other textiles) and 6307.90.98 (other made-up articles) applies with or without a USMCA claim. No Chapter 63 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian made-ups pay nothing extra with USMCA except the five Section 338 subheadings, which pay 50% (60% without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.exemption: Thailand has no exception list for Chapter 63; worn clothing is exempt (note 52(b)). GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Thai made-ups pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwan pays 10% in total in place of the base rate (note 52(k)), so lines with a base rate of 10% or more pay only the base rate. Taiwan's exception list (note 52(j)) names no Chapter 63 subheading. Narrow woven ribbons from Taiwan remain under an antidumping order. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese made-ups pay 10% in total, or the base rate where it is higher.

inEffect.exemption: South Korea pays 12.5% in total in place of the base rate (note 52(k)), KORUS claim or not, so lines with a base rate above 12.5% (14.9%, 20.9%) pay only the base rate. Korea has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Korean blankets, towels and bedding pay 12.5% in total.

inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (SPI P) are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95): that covers 6301–6309 lines that print P. Lines whose General rate is Free carry no P and are not entered under CAFTA-DR, so they pay 12.5%, as do rags and scrap of 6310, which are outside the textile-goods definition. The Section 122 surcharge also exempted CAFTA-DR textile goods (9903.03.09) before it expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Dominican sheets, towels, curtains and other made-ups that qualify under CAFTA-DR enter with no duty at all; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every line but worn clothing (note 50(a)(ii)); the 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian towels and bed linen pay 37.5% on top of the base rate.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Russia (rates in lieu of column 2)
inEffect.exemption: Russian goods on 17 lines (cotton blankets, knitted bed linen, some cotton sheets and cotton damask table linen) pay 35% in place of the column 2 rate (9903.90.08, U.S. note 30); all Russian goods pay the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty except worn clothing.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian made-ups pay the column 2 rate (or 35%) plus 12.5%; trade is negligible.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (43: Algeria, Angola, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, …)
inEffect.exemption: Jordan's exception list (note 52(j), 9903.06.20) covers every Chapter 63 subheading. Guatemala and El Salvador lists cover every subheading when CAFTA-DR is claimed (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09). CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). No other country list names a Chapter 63 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Jordanian and CAFTA-DR-claimed Central American made-ups pay none.

changes.detail: All 229 Chapter 63 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 63 this keeps +7.5% (9903.88.15) on 75 subheadings, including cotton sheets, towels, pillowcases and worn clothing.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 63
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles over 800 cc from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 63 line is on their annexes.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; Chapter 63 entries unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 changed the products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026. None of the five Chapter 63 subheadings was removed; Revision 21 still lists 6303.92.20 (synthetic curtains), 6305.33.00 (polyethylene/polypropylene sacks), 6306.12.00 (synthetic tarpaulins), 6306.19.21 (tarpaulins of other textiles) and 6307.90.98 (other made-up articles) in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Narrow woven ribbons from Taiwan: 83.67% antidumping rate
changes.detail: Commerce's final results for September 2023–August 2024 set an 83.67% antidumping margin for Lace Fashions Industrial and Trydent. The ribbon orders on China and Taiwan (2010, continued March 2022) list 6307.90.98.91 among the statistical numbers ribbons may enter under, so cut ribbon put up as a made-up article can still be subject merchandise.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on five Chapter 63 subheadings
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in U.S. note 51(b)(3), which names 6303.92.20 (synthetic curtains), 6305.33.00 (polyethylene/polypropylene sacks), 6306.12.00 (synthetic tarpaulins), 6306.19.21 (tarpaulins of other textiles) and 6307.90.98 (other made-up articles) — 22 statistical lines. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach 227 of 229 lines
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) — 10% for India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Mexico and Canada, 12.5% for China, Vietnam, Türkiye and Thailand, 10% in total for the EU. Worn clothing (6309.00.00) is on the general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86). Jordan's list covers every Chapter 63 subheading, and Guatemala's and El Salvador's cover them when CAFTA-DR is claimed; CAFTA-DR textile goods are exempt (note 52(i)). USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). Worn clothing (6309.00.00) is the only Chapter 63 subheading on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance: cotton products are a high-priority sector
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance for importers lists the supply-chain tracing documents it expects for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, which include cotton and cotton products and apparel. Cotton sheets, towels, blankets and other cotton made-ups are presumed barred if made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity, unless the importer rebuts the presumption.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 63 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08) and CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free (9903.03.09) were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. AGOA (SPI D) is printed on only seven Chapter 63 lines — silk bed linen, hand-loomed and jute wall hangings, wool pillow covers, some air mattresses, wall banners and 6307.90.98 — but heading 9819.11.33 lets textile articles of Chapter 63 wholly formed in lesser-developed AGOA countries enter Free. GSP remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: China: 50% on textile face masks and respirators
changes.detail: The 2024 four-year review raised the Section 301 rate on Chinese N95 respirators (6307.90.98.42/.44), other textile respirators (.50) and textile face masks (.70/.75) to +50% (9903.91.07), replacing the 25% that applied to disposable masks during 2025.

changes.title: Nepal Preference Program (NP) expired
changes.detail: The program that let Nepal ship listed goods duty-free (SPI NP) ended after December 31, 2025. NP is still printed on 6301.90.00 (other blankets) and 6308.00.00 (needlecraft sets), but no longer applies.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 63 line; CAFTA-DR-originating made-ups are not covered.

changes.title: China List 4A exclusions extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions, including four in Chapter 63: knitted polyester dust covers for mattresses and pillows (6302.10.00.20), zippered full-encasement cotton pillow protectors (6302.31.90.40), and instant cold packs with a textile lining and cotton laparotomy sponges (6307.90.98.91). They remove the 7.5% List 4A duty (9903.88.69) but not the 12.5% 2026 duty.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 63 line on top of List 4A until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025: 50% in all on Indian sheets and towels. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates, for example India +25%, Vietnam +20%, Pakistan and Cambodia +19%, Bangladesh +20%, and 15% in total for EU goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for 90 days (later extended). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125%, on top of List 4A and the fentanyl duty.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 63 subheading was on the exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of List 4A.

changes.title: Laminated woven sacks from China: orders continued
changes.detail: After the third sunset reviews, Commerce continued the 2008 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on laminated woven sacks from China — printed, laminated sacks of woven polypropylene or polyethylene strip up to 1 kg, the kind used for pet food and seed (6305.33.00.40, .80). CBP keeps collecting cash deposits at the rates in effect at entry.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China: 25% on disposable textile face masks
changes.detail: The 2024 four-year review put +25% (9903.91.04) on disposable textile face masks of China (6307.90.98.70) for 2025; it was replaced by the 50% heading on January 1, 2026.

changes.title: Laminated woven sacks from Vietnam: orders continued
changes.detail: After the first sunset reviews, Commerce continued the 2019 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on laminated woven sacks from Vietnam (6305.33.00.40, .80), which cover sacks made in Vietnam whatever the origin of the fabric.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 63 goods were **$16.18B in 2025**, 10.6% less than the $18.09B of 2024 and about half the $31.08B of 2020, when textile face masks and protective goods surged. **China** shipped **$7.05B** (44%), down 25% from $9.37B; its largest heading is 6307 (other made-up articles, $2.99B), then bed and bath linen ($1.58B) and blankets ($1.11B). **India** ($3.06B) and **Pakistan** ($1.62B) ship mainly sheets and towels of heading 6302; **Mexico** ($1.26B) ships other made-ups and curtains.

By product, heading 6302 (bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen) was $5.59B and 6307 $5.38B — two-thirds of the chapter. The largest single lines were 6307.90 other made-up articles ($4.56B), **cotton terry towels** 6302.60 ($2.01B), unprinted cotton bed linen 6302.31 ($1.18B), synthetic blankets 6301.40 ($1.10B) and synthetic curtains 6303.92 ($1.03B).

Imports shifted away from China in 2025, when Chinese goods carried List 4A, the IEEPA fentanyl duty and, from April, the reciprocal tariff: Vietnam rose 42% to $689M, Cambodia 67% to $237M and Thailand 49%. Those IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies to most suppliers instead, and China keeps List 4A. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on a sheet, towel or tarp depends as much on **where its fabric was made** as on the line. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026): **India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Cambodia +10%**, **Vietnam, Türkiye and Thailand +12.5%**, EU and Taiwanese goods 10% in total and Korean goods 12.5% in total. **China pays +20%** on most lines (12.5% plus List 4A), +12.5% on lines not on List 4A and +62.5% on masks. **USMCA goods from Mexico pay nothing extra**, and Canada pays 50% on five Section 338 subheadings even with USMCA.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Bed Linen, Towels, Tarps & Other Made-Up Textiles (HTS Ch. 63): Origin Rules, Labeling & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Home Textiles: Origin Rules, UFLPA, FTC Labeling & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Chapter 63) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, FTC and CPSC rules for each HTS Chapter 63 line — textile country of origin (fabric-formed rule, 19 CFR 102.21), manufacturer ID, fibre-content labels, UFLPA for cotton, AD/CVD on woven sacks — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, CAFTA-DR, exception lists, China exclusions, first sale, drawback and FTZs.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For most Chapter 63 goods **the country of origin is where the fabric was woven or knitted, not where it was cut and sewn** (19 CFR 102.21): Pakistani fabric sewn into sheets in another country is still Pakistani. Some man-made-fibre items (for example polyester sheets, curtains and bedspreads) take the origin of the country that dyed and printed the fabric with two finishing steps; worn clothing and rags are from where they were last collected and packed. Every entry must name the manufacturer by manufacturer identification code, cotton goods face the UFLPA presumption, and sheets, towels, blankets and curtains sold at retail need fibre-content and origin labels (16 CFR part 303).

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: **USMCA** for goods cut and sewn in North America from regional fabric, **CAFTA-DR** for Central American made-ups (also exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty), **Jordan's** exception list, the **China List 4A exclusions** where the goods fit, **first-sale valuation**, **drawback** and **foreign-trade zones**. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Know where the fabric was made — that is usually the country of origin
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: +10% for India or Pakistan, +12.5% for Vietnam, +20% for China (62.5% on masks)
levers.appliesTo: Headings 6301–6306, 6307.10, 6307.90 and 6308 (fabric-formed rule); 6307.20 is where assembled; 6309–6310 where collected and packed
levers.document: Mill records showing where the fabric was formed (woven or knitted), and for 102.21(e)(2) goods where it was dyed, printed and finished; the MID of that producer on the entry.
levers.caveat: Moving the cut-and-sew step does not move origin when the fabric stays the same: sheets sewn in Cambodia from Chinese fabric are Chinese. Cotton goods and blends with 16% or more cotton always follow the fabric-formed rule.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on made-ups cut and sewn in Mexico or Canada from regional fabric
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada plus the base rate (up to 20.9%)
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for goods that qualify as originating: fabric (and yarn) from the USMCA region, and the good cut (or knit to shape) and sewn or otherwise assembled there (General Note 11, Chapter 63 rules)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: Asian fabric sewn in Mexico does not qualify. For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 6303.92.20 (synthetic curtains), 6305.33.00 (polyethylene/polypropylene sacks), 6306.12.00 (synthetic tarpaulins), 6306.19.21 (tarpaulins of other textiles) and 6307.90.98 (other made-up articles). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Claim CAFTA-DR — it also removes the 2026 Section 301 duty
levers.saves: The base rate and the 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty on Central American and Dominican made-ups
levers.appliesTo: Textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua that originate under General Note 29 (fabric formed in the region, cut and sewn there) and are entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (SPI P)
levers.document: Proof of origin under CAFTA-DR and the SPI "P" on the entry line; for Guatemala and El Salvador the exemption heading 9903.06.06 or 9903.06.09, for the others 9903.05.95.
levers.caveat: Non-originating Nicaraguan goods will pay 10% from 2027 and 15% from 2028 (9903.89.01).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Claim another FTA, AGOA or the Haiti made-up provision where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate — up to 20.9% on cotton bed linen, 9.1% on terry towels; for Jordan, the Section 301 duty too
levers.appliesTo: Goods of Jordan, Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman and Singapore under each agreement's yarn- or fabric-forward rule; AGOA lesser-developed countries (9819.11.33, through December 31, 2026); listed made-up articles wholly assembled in Haiti (9820.63.05)
levers.document: The origin proof each program requires and the SPI on the entry line (JO, KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, MA, BH, OM, SG, D), or the Chapter 98 heading.
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)) except for Jordan's list and CAFTA-DR; Chapter 98 entries such as 9819.11.33 and 9820.63.05 are outside it. GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020 and the Nepal program (NP) since December 31, 2025, although both codes are still printed.

levers.title: Use a China List 4A exclusion where the goods match it
levers.saves: The 7.5% List 4A duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Knitted polyester mattress and pillow dust covers (6302.10.00.20), zippered full-encasement cotton pillow protectors (6302.31.90.40), instant cold packs with textile lining and cotton laparotomy sponges (6307.90.98.91), entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with the statistical number, and records showing the goods match the exclusion's description.
levers.caveat: Exclusions are narrow and end after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends them again.

levers.title: Check the classification line by line — trim, nap, print and fibre move the rate
levers.saves: Up to 18 points of base rate: cotton sheets with embroidery or piping are 20.9%, without trim 6.7%, napped printed 2.5%; stuffed items leave the chapter for 9404
levers.appliesTo: Bed linen (6302.21–.32), bedspreads (6304.19), towels (6302.60 vs. 6302.91) and any set or blend
levers.document: A binding ruling request to CBP (19 CFR part 177) with fibre content by weight, construction, trim and finish; invoices must state the fibre content (19 CFR 141.89).
levers.caveat: Classification follows the goods as imported: removing trim only to change the line, then adding it after import, is not a lawful plan. Rulings bind only the transaction described.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 63 and Section XI notes

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty — base rate and Section 301 — is charged on a lower value when the mill's price to a trading company is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company, agent-buyer or brand owner rather than straight from the maker
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the factory invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry.

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods are exported or destroyed
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on made-ups re-exported unused or used to make exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

levers.title: Hold, kit or relabel goods in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on goods re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until goods enter the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for bedding and towels distributed to Canada, Mexico and the U.S. from one stock
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Goods entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date.

rules.title: Textile country of origin: for 6301–6306, 6307.10 and 6307.90 the country where the fabric was formed; for listed man-made-fibre bed linen, curtains and furnishings (6302.22, .29, .53, .59, .93, .99, 6303.92, .99, 6304.19, .93, .99) the country that dyed and printed the fabric with two finishing operations; 6307.20 where wholly assembled; 6309–6310 where last collected and packed

Entry is denied for textiles from a company named in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details for textile fibre products: each fibre by generic name and percentage by weight, the manufacturer, and the country where processed or made

Textile Act labels on bedding, curtains and draperies, tablecloths and napkins, towels, washcloths and dish cloths, afghans and throws, cushions, sleeping bags and flags: fibre content, the RN or company name, and the country where made. Secondhand household textiles and disposable nonwovens are excluded
Wool Products Labeling Act: wool and cashmere blankets and throws must show wool fibre content and origin

Mattress pads (a mat or ticking filled with resilient material) must pass the cigarette-ignition standard; most such pads are stuffed and classified in heading 9404, while unfilled mattress covers and protectors of 6302/6304 are outside the standard

UFLPA: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it; cotton and cotton products are a high-priority sector, so cotton sheets, towels and blankets need cotton tracing documents

Antidumping and countervailing duty cash deposits on laminated woven sacks from China (A-570-916, C-570-917) and Vietnam (A-552-823, C-552-824): printed, laminated sacks of woven PP/PE strip up to 1 kg, classified in 6305.33.00.40 and .80
Antidumping (China, Taiwan) and countervailing (China) duties on narrow woven ribbons with woven selvedge; the orders list 6307.90.98.91 among the numbers ribbons may enter under
Country-of-origin marking on the article or its retail container; bales of worn clothing in bulk are marked on the bale or container

groups.label: Blankets and traveling rugs (incl. electric blankets)
groups.note: Origin is where the blanket fabric was formed. Wool and cashmere blankets need Wool Act labels; stuffed quilts and comforters are heading 9404, not here.

groups.label: Bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen (sheets, pillowcases, towels)
groups.note: Origin is where the fabric was woven or knitted — except man-made-fibre bed, table and toilet linen of 6302.22, .29, .53, .59, .93 and .99, which takes the origin of the dye-print-finish country if that happened. Cotton goods need UFLPA cotton tracing.

groups.label: Curtains, drapes and interior blinds
groups.note: Curtains take the origin of the fabric; synthetic curtains (6303.92) can take the dye-print-finish country. 6303.92.20 is on Canada's 50% Section 338 list.

groups.label: Bedspreads and other furnishing articles (not stuffed)
groups.note: Furnishings that are not stuffed. Origin follows the fabric (or dye-print-finish for 6304.19, .93, .99). Filled mattress pads are 9404 and must meet 16 CFR part 1632.

groups.label: Sacks and bags for packing goods (incl. FIBCs, woven PP sacks)
groups.note: Origin follows the fabric. Laminated woven sacks from China and Vietnam (6305.33.00.40/.80) are under AD/CVD orders; 6305.33.00 is on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Tarpaulins, awnings, tents, sails, camping goods
groups.note: Tarps and tents take the origin of the fabric. Synthetic and other tarpaulins (6306.12, 6306.19.21) are on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Other made-up articles (cleaning cloths, masks, flags, pet toys)
groups.note: Origin follows the fabric for 6307.10 and 6307.90; lifejackets (6307.20) are from where assembled. Chinese masks and respirators pay 50% Section 301; 6307.90.98 is on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Needlecraft sets (fabric and yarn for rugs, tapestries)
groups.note: Origin is where the woven fabric component was formed.

groups.label: Worn clothing and other worn textile articles
groups.note: Worn clothing must show appreciable wear and be entered in bulk, bales or sacks. Origin is where it was last collected and packed. Exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(b)).

groups.label: Rags, scrap twine, cordage and rope
groups.note: Rags and scrap are from where they were last collected and packed.

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 63 FAQ: HS Codes & Import Tariffs for Bed Sheets, Towels, Blankets, Tarps & Used Clothing

seo.title: Bed Sheet, Towel, Blanket & Used Clothing HS Code and Tariff FAQ 2026 (HTS Chapter 63) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing made-up textiles: the HS code for bed sheets, pillowcases, towels, blankets, curtains, tarpaulins, tents, face masks and used clothing, and the 2026 tariffs from China, India and Pakistan.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing made-up textile articles into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 63 base rates run from Free to 20.9% and are unchanged since January 2025: cotton terry towels 9.1%, printed cotton sheets 6.7%, polyester sheets 11.4%, synthetic tarps 8.8%. The extra duty by country often costs more.

Since July 24, 2026 India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Cambodia pay 10% Section 301 on top of the base rate, Vietnam and Türkiye 12.5%, EU suppliers 10% in total. China pays 20% on most lines (12.5% plus List 4A), 12.5% on synthetic blankets, sheets and tarps, and 62.5% on masks and respirators.
Worn clothing (6309) is Free and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty for every country; only China's 7.5% List 4A applies.

Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on synthetic curtains, plastic-strip sacks, tarpaulins and 6307.90.98, even with USMCA. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

Origin follows the fabric: the country that wove or knitted it, not where it was sewn (19 CFR 102.21). Cotton goods face the UFLPA presumption, and laminated woven sacks from China and Vietnam pay AD/CVD.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 63 cover?
faqs.answer: Made-up textile articles: blankets (6301), bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen (6302), curtains (6303), bedspreads and furnishings (6304), packing sacks (6305), tarpaulins, tents and sails (6306), other made-ups such as cleaning cloths, flags and face masks (6307), needlecraft sets (6308), worn clothing (6309) and rags (6310). Garments are chapters 61–62; stuffed pillows and comforters are 9404.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for bed sheets, pillowcases and duvet covers?
faqs.answer: Heading 6302. Knitted bed linen is 6302.10 (6%). Woven printed bed linen is 6302.21 (cotton) or 6302.22 (man-made fibres); unprinted is 6302.31 or 6302.32. Plain cotton sheets are 6.7% (not napped) or 3.8%–2.5% (napped); with embroidery, lace or piping 11.9%–20.9%; polyester sheets 11.4%, 14.9% with trim. Pillowcases and duvet covers are statistical lines within the same subheadings.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for towels?
faqs.answer: Cotton terry towels (bath, beach, hand and dish) are 6302.60.00 at 9.1%; other cotton towels 6302.91.00 (9.2%); man-made-fibre towels 6302.93 (6.2% pile, 9.9% other). Paper towels are chapter 48. From Pakistan or India a cotton terry towel pays 19.1% in all; from China 29.1%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for blankets and throws?
faqs.answer: Heading 6301: electric blankets 6301.10 (11.4%), wool 6301.20 (Free), cotton 6301.30 (8.4%), synthetic fibres such as fleece 6301.40 (8.5%), other 6301.90 (7.2%). Quilts and comforters that are stuffed are bedding of 9404. Chinese cotton blankets pay 20% extra; synthetic and electric blankets 12.5%, since they are not on List 4A.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for curtains and drapes?
faqs.answer: Heading 6303: knitted curtains 6303.12–6303.19, woven cotton 6303.91 (10.3%), synthetic 6303.92 (11.3%), other 6303.99 (11.3%). Textile shower curtains are here; plastic ones are chapter 39. Canada's synthetic curtains (6303.92.20) pay a 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for tarpaulins and tents?
faqs.answer: Textile tarpaulins, awnings and sunblinds are 6306.12 (synthetic, 8.8%) and 6306.19; tents and canopies 6306.22 (synthetic: backpacking tents Free, others 8.8%) and 6306.29. Tarps of plastic film or sheeting, as most PE tarps are, are chapter 39. Chinese synthetic tarps pay 12.5% extra; Canadian ones 50% under Section 338.

faqs.question: What goes in HS code 6307.90?
faqs.answer: 6307.90 is other made-up articles: labels, cords, surgical drapes, pet toys, wall banners and the catch-all 6307.90.98 (7%), which holds flags, textile face masks and respirators, and many others. 6307.10 is floor cloths, dishcloths and dusters; 6307.20 lifejackets. Chinese textile masks and respirators pay 50% Section 301 plus 12.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for used clothing, and is there a tariff?
faqs.answer: 6309.00.00, Free. It covers clothing, blankets, linen, furnishings, footwear and headgear that show appreciable wear and are entered in bulk, bales or sacks; worn goods imported otherwise go to their own headings. 6309 is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty for all countries; only Chinese worn clothing pays 7.5% (List 4A).

faqs.question: Are tote bags and shopping bags in Chapter 63?
faqs.answer: No. Heading 4202 names shopping bags, and textile articles of 4202 are excluded from Section XI. Chapter 63 keeps only sacks and bags used to pack goods (6305): jute Free, cotton 6.2%, FIBC bulk bags and woven polypropylene sacks 8.4%.

faqs.question: Are there antidumping duties on laminated woven sacks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Printed laminated sacks of woven polypropylene or polyethylene strip up to 1 kg (6305.33.00.40/.80) from China (orders since 2008, continued February 2025) and Vietnam (since 2019, continued November 2024) pay antidumping and countervailing cash deposits on top of the 8.4% base rate and Section 301.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on textiles and home textiles from China in 2026?
faqs.answer: For Chapter 63, every line but worn clothing pays 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31). 75 of 99 subheadings — cotton sheets, towels, tablecloths, curtains of cotton, most bags and tarps of cotton — also pay 7.5% under List 4A, so 20% on top of the base rate; textile masks and respirators pay 50% plus 12.5%. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on home textiles from India and Pakistan?
searchedAs: tariff on textiles from india to usa
us tariff on textiles from india
bed sheets hs code in pakistan
faqs.answer: Both pay the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (India 9903.05.44, Pakistan 9903.05.62), with no exception list: 19.1% on cotton terry towels, 16.7% on printed cotton sheets. India's 50% IEEPA rate of late 2025 ended in February 2026; GSP has been expired since 2020.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import made-up textiles from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $16.18B of Chapter 63 goods: China $7.05B (44%, down 25% on 2024), India $3.06B (19%), Pakistan $1.62B (10%), Mexico $1.26B, then Vietnam, Türkiye, Cambodia and Bangladesh. India and Pakistan ship mostly towels and bed linen; China's largest heading is 6307, other made-up articles.

faqs.question: How is the country of origin of sheets and towels determined?
faqs.answer: By CBP's textile rules (19 CFR 102.21): for most Chapter 63 goods, the country where the fabric was woven or knitted, not where it was cut and sewn. Some man-made-fibre linens and furnishings take the origin of the country that dyed and printed the fabric with two finishing steps. The origin decides the Section 301 rate and the label.
